\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Dependent variable: growth of real GDP per capita (\%, five-year average), 1979--2023; all regressors in t\_p $-$ 1, the last year of the previous period. Predetermined controls: log GDP per capita, human capital, investment, openness, inflation, population growth and commodity terms-of-trade growth, all in t\_p $-$ 1. Column 1: preferred H1 specification, country and period fixed effects, standard errors clustered by country. Column 2: two-step system GMM with lagged growth, the wage bill and initial income instrumented by lags 2--3 (lagged growth: lags 1--2), collapsed, other controls and period dummies as standard instruments; Windmeijer-corrected standard errors. Column 3: bias-corrected fixed effects (Breitung, Kripfganz and Hayakawa, 2022), which assumes the controls are strictly exogenous; robust standard errors. Columns 4--6: wage bill as a share of total expenditure (expense plus net investment in non-financial assets); column 4 holds total expenditure constant; columns 5--6 add the shares of goods and services, interest, other expense and either public investment (5) or transfers (6), total expenditure and revenue, so the wage-bill coefficient measures a reallocation of one percentage point of spending from the omitted category; the fiscal balance is implied. Shares, revenue and expenditure follow the extended cleaning rules (Table A1). Wild cluster bootstrap: Webb weights, 9,999 replications, clustered by country. Countries row: clusters (columns 1, 4--6) or groups (columns 2--3). * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01.\end{minipage}

The negative-gap model is summarised by its average effect, the coefficient after a positive gap plus the interaction times the share of negative gaps (0.40). Bootstrap p: wild cluster bootstrap by country (Webb weights, 9,999 replications; WRE for 2SLS). Differences from the preferred estimate: country pairs bootstrap, the same 999 draws for every variant. Null-adjusted estimates: observed coefficient minus the mean of 1,000 simulations of a zero-effect wage bill (mean-reverting design of Table A4, panel B, or calibrated anchored design of Table A4, panel E), with the simulated ratios replacing the observed ones (also in the instruments); the CI comes from the same pairs-bootstrap draws, each re-estimating the observed coefficient and running one new simulation on the resampled countries, so that it combines sampling and simulation error. Leave one period out: the preferred specification on its full sample, dropping each period in turn, clustered standard errors. Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the third addendum).\end{minipage}

First reporting period: the first period in which the country has the GFS wage bill in t\_p $-$ 1. Differences in means: regression on an indicator of the 44, standard errors clustered by country. Group coefficients: the wage bill interacted with the group indicator; wild cluster bootstrap p of the interaction (Webb weights, 9,999 replications). Share explained: [β(355) $-$ β(355 without the block)] / [β(355) $-$ β(311)]. Full-sample checks: growth before the period is the average growth of period p $-$ 1 or, when that period is missing, the mean annual growth of the five years before t\_p (13 country-periods recovered); each variant is compared with the preferred specification on the same observations. Simulated nulls: observed minus the mean of 1,000 simulations of a zero-effect wage bill (mean-reverting design; anchored design with unscaled residuals; anchored design with the moment-matched k of Table A4, panel H, at ε = 0.48); 95\% CI from 999 country pairs-bootstrap draws, each re-estimating the observed coefficient and running one new simulation on the resampled countries. Transition economies (former Soviet Union, Central and Eastern Europe, Balkans), periods starting before 1999: 3 of the 355 country-periods (BGR, HUN and SVN 1994); blocks are dropped only among the 44 lost country-periods, so the transition block is one country-period (SVN 1994, N = 354), whereas Table A9 drops all three (N = 352). Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the fourth addendum).\end{minipage}
